questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that I was going somewhere where I could enhance my spanish abilities and where I had a possiblity of interacting with people that spoke spanish

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to find the necessary information upon arrival. Many essential things were communicated at an individual meeting in the office of the university the first week of arrival, but essential things, such as it being mandatory to book an appointment for this meeting and logging your arrival within a certain amount of time, were things I didn't know when I arrived and only found out gradually or by coincidence. So the beginning of the stay was a bit chaotic and confusing, especially since a lot of the information and forms aren't online

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some e-mails on my KU mail from my host university and then I had a meeting at the host university which gave me further information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Universidad de Barcelona where I studied didn't offer the possibility to live on campus so you have to find off campus housing. You can be lucky and find a really good room very fast or you can spend a long time looking. The housing in Barcelona functions with rapid changes and in a way where you have to be prepared to say yes right away if you like a place. Unfortunately, it often happens that someone else might already have gotten the room before you. A lot of places you can move in from day to day and there's no contracts which makes room for a lot of flexibility. Idealista is the place to look and beware of scammers on Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Since off campus was the only option available in my situation I would say it's nice since it gives you the possibility to interact and become friends with people from outside the university. It also gives you the possiblity to choose which area you prefer to live in since some of the campus' are situated a bit outside of the centre or if you prefer to live close to the beach

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to a meeting at the office of the university the first week of being in Barcelona to log my arrival. After that university started and we had two weeks to try out different courses before choosing our final ones. The week after the try out period being over I went to another meeting at the office of the university where the courses where officially approved (if you have courses outside of your own faculty you have to get them approved by the faculty your taking them at before this meeting). After that I went to another part of the university where my matriculation was completed which gave me access to the virtual campus and provided me with a university email. It was only after the last meeting that I had access to all material and my courses at the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could contact the Erasmus office at the university by email or you could walk by to ask them for help. There was not a lot of information available online and most is in catalan or spanish.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would have prefered courses in my own subject, but most of the classes were offered in catalan and the ones that were in spanish overlapped in the timetable. Therefore, I had to choose one course in catalan and two courses outside of my own field which were both interesting and challenging.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of picking classes outside of your own field or faculty, and if you really think a course would be interesting, but it's in catalan, then take it anyways. If you know some spanish, you can pick up on a lot of the catalan after a little bit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A bit lower level than in the ones I had in Copenhagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching took place in class rooms rather than lecture halls which I was used to from home. We didn't have classes with tutors like in Copenhagen, but instead each course had practical classes assigned to them apart from the normal lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Anthropology and feminism, Political Philosophy I, Geografia Humana, Visual Anthropology, History of Contemporary America

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my visual anthropology course even though it was in catalan. Our professor was easy to understand and used a lot of english material and he was very inclusive and inspiring as a teacher. Other than that he was very accomodating and aware that we were a couple of Erasmus students in his class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs as such

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most items in Barcelona are cheaper than in Denmark. There's more of a culture for going out eating and having drinks than meeting in peoples' homes like we do at home so that naturally means that I ended up spending more money on going out than I would do at home - but it was exactly like it was supposed to be and definitely worth it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know that you could pay a fee that gave you access to a wide range of sports activities by the university, but I only heard about it through friends and too late to apply to it myself. Since I was there during corona there weren't any social activities arranged by the university

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in non-academic activities arranged by the university. I used the app Meet Up a couple of times and then I became part of some Whatsapp groups for the faculty where people would occasionally meet up and share information

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Costa Brava, Montserrat, hike around Montseny, go to Valencia and the Pyrenees and take advantage of all the cultural offers that a vibrant city like Barcelona has to offer. Also just enjoy the city. Time passes by too quickly when you have your normal day life somewhere and in the end you haven't done half of the things that you would have liked to

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy adjusting to the local culture since Barcelona is a very international city and people are from all over the world

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to interact with them in class or ask for their numbers. They are very nice once you talk to them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. My spanish weren't the best when I arrived, but everyone speaks english anyways

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very sociable and easy to interact with which I appreciate a lot. People are willing to meet new people and don't look weird at you if you strike up a conversation with them. I also liked the eating and drinking out a lot cause it gives the possibility of trying out new things and makes it easier to meet new people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It might sound like the university part was challenging and that the bureaucratic side lacked a lot of things and wasn't informative, but it's all worth it. I love Barcelona and the people I met there. So just go for it and don't get frustrated if you can't find somewhere to live at first or if you can't get the exact courses that you want cause there's so many other things that's gonna give you amazing experiences once you're there

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people that I did

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The level of spanish and the way they evaluate your performance continually

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
